chapter: 52nd Street, Birdland and the bop musicians
title: Oscar Pettiford, composing and the Moscow Mule
summary: With Pettiford she composed several tunes a night; his drinking led her to move him to cello and hire Percy Heath.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But you just can't shift from the East Side -

Well, you can, but you can't shift overnight; you have to rehearse with them. We went in there and started blowing. Oscar was great to play with because we composed at least 3 tunes a night or more. He'd start a bass figure and I would play, and that is really my schtick, my whole way of doing. I like to compose while I'm playing. We had a great session going except then he was crazy about his "Moscow Mule". He'd go around the corner on Eighth Avenue and I'd have to go to get him. So one night I got a stick and I hit him on his knee and I said, "Listen, you had too much Moscow Mule." He laughed about it, you know, and I decided to put him on cello. So I called in Percy Heath, for bass, a terrific bass player also. So one night I was blowing like mad. Oscar was on the cello, he turned around and said, "You don't blow like that with me." I said, "Yes, because you high off of Moscow Mule." So I did put the musicians back to work there in this particular club. Charlie Parker came in one night and he said to me, "Lou, let's get a band or something together. You know all the cats always want me to get a band with you."
